judge-football.justification: Day-3/UDFA pool is the headline, with a 13-name 2026 shortlist carrying P(2026 SOE>0) beside a pick-and-routes baseline, and two drill-vs-tape disagreement cases (Boutte, Bond) with coaching and board actions. Edge is thin (7/13 vs 6/13; rank-correlation interval includes zero): a tiebreaker, not a rule. Confounders handled: opportunity, alignment, QB, sample size, drill repeatability, Bayesian errors-in-variables bound, clustered intervals, time-forward folds. Gaps: injuries, 40 clip-start. Unique: drill-to-game cut force with same code; persistent-SOE-vs-pick framing; shortlist half is a conventional persistence check. Terminology correct; minor loose phrases.
top_changes: Resolve weak headline evidence (rank-correlation 0.37 vs 0.06 in abstract vs +0.31 [-0.08,0.63] in table; yes/no gap 8 pts [-16,27]); lead with SOE persistence as tiebreaker only; one labelled line for all-rounds result (0.33 [0.13,0.53], 2 of 2 folds).
Add a worked decision case on a real board (two day-3 receivers, similar pick and routes) with roster/dollar consequence, and a 2026 Combine protocol note on which drills to double-rep.

Cut headline complexity (move ridge, QB rows to appendix); add scheme and injury context to the shortlist (games missed, slot vs outside for Washington, Douglas, Tez Johnson); mention the 40 clip-start issue.

judge-datascience.justification: Spot-checked: n=116 WR/TE with Break G (82 WR, 34 TE); 13-name shortlist, 7 negative Break G; Spearman Break G vs SOE -0.07; numbers.json consistent with text (1,987 words, 4 figures, check.py clean). Not reproduced: clustered/Bayesian intervals and leave-one-season-out. Strengths: fixed no-tracking baseline, out-of-class validation, standardization, shrinkage, honest weak day-3 result. Weaknesses: tiny day-3 pool (20 pairs, 16 receivers), pre-specified framing relies on trust, no mixed models, survivor bias from 100-route cutoff, drill-to-game link untestable on sample, 2025 class single season.
top_changes: Address survivorship with a selection model (P(100+ routes) from pick and Break G, IPW) and report exclusions.
Strengthen day-3 evidence with a receiver random-intercept mixed model and a permutation test of the 7/13 vs 6/13 gap; report shortlist calibration.
Table of Break G slopes across plain, ridge, no-offset forecasts with a single TOST bound at +3 in.

judge-writeup.justification: check.py passes: 1,875 words, 4 figures, 5 tables. Structure near finalist pattern; pool and interval now stated honestly, fixing round-13 overclaim. Problems: 25-word two-sentence title; ~85-word lede stacking four statistics and two intervals; 0.37 vs 0.06 vs +0.31 not reconciled; motivation opens on a scouting cliche; appendix-style detail in body (2.8-to-1 Bayes factor, reliability, 88% resample win rate, all-rounds secondary pool); hedge stacks; split story; Break G definition not one coach sentence; analyst terms (rank correlation, shrunk, Youden, Brier).
top_changes: Short title and a lede of at most 60 words; move yes/no count and rank-correlation interval to the table.
Move analyst-only detail to the appendix; collapse hedges into one verdict; reconcile 0.37 vs 0.06 with +0.31.
Rewrite Why it matters and The metric: roster decision, why now, one-sentence metric.
